cursor_checkpoint_atomicity.mechanism: data-before-metadata ordering: PacketSink writes the packet file through atomic_bytes (exclusive .pending -> write -> fsync(file) -> os.replace -> fsync(dir)) and only then does the caller commit cursor + identities + sink state in ONE SQLite transaction (INSERT OR REPLACE + single commit, PRAGMA synchronous=FULL).
cursor_checkpoint_atomicity.invariant: PacketSink._append_packet closes the PREVIOUS file before appending the new packet (align-places-common.py:280-281 vs 285-299), so the buffer committed by every save_cursor() is exactly the content of the file that will be closed next. That is why the single-file `allowed_orphan` test in the resume gate (places_checkpoint.py:84-87) is sufficient rather than optimistic.
cursor_checkpoint_atomicity.finalClose: double-protected: save_cursor() before sink.close() persists the exact final buffer, then sink.close() writes it, then save_cursor() records it (align-places-common.py:446-448).
cursor_checkpoint_atomicity.identitiesWithCursor: add_identity deliberately does NOT commit (places_checkpoint.py:98-102), so uncommitted identities roll back together with the cursor; the resume gate cross-checks COUNT(identities) == sum(input_counts) (places_checkpoint.py:93-96).
cursor_checkpoint_atomicity.independentDemonstration: see adversarialFixture below — a crash in the close->commit window on a NON-FIRST file recovered byte-identically.

duplicate_identity_across_restart.evidence: identities live in the same SQLite file as the cursor with PRIMARY KEY(source, record); add_identity maps sqlite3.IntegrityError to ValueError naming the (source, record) key. A replay after resume therefore still raises, and the gateway check refuses a DB whose identity count does not match the recorded input counts, so a partially committed or foreign DB fails closed.
duplicate_identity_across_restart.note: rejection aborts the run rather than skipping the record — consistent with the doc's 'persisted duplicate rejection'. The check is per-checkpoint (global), not per input file (N2).

source_pin_binding.evidence: pins bind curated root, EVERY input file's bytes+sha256, output path, schema digest, contract digest, implementation digest (align-places-common.py), checkpointImplementation digest (places_checkpoint.py) and the packet options plus createdAt (align-places-common.py:364-370); resume compares the whole dict and refuses on any mismatch (places_checkpoint.py:71-74). Any byte change to either implementation invalidates resume, which is precisely why these immutable bytes matter. Input files are re-hashed and per-asset digests re-verified before use.

interruption_corruption_handling.evidence: missing, extra, truncated and corrupt retained assets are each refused by the resume gate; a leftover .pending in packets/ is enumerated by the 'all files' scan, is not the allowed orphan key, and therefore fails closed with 'explicit recovery required' and is never deleted (the untested half of the doc's claim, verified by code reading); the writer lock uses O_EXCL and unlinks only after an (st_dev, st_ino) identity check, so a replaced lock is never removed by a stale holder; legacy partials without a pinned checkpoint are refused; previously accepted packages are immutable.
interruption_corruption_handling.scopeLimit: the lock guards ONE destination, as the doc itself discloses; one-writer discipline across paths remains a coordinator obligation.

findings.observed: the doc states a closed file 'is reusable only if it equals the exact saved buffer', which reads as conditional. By construction the saved buffer is ALWAYS exactly the next file to be closed (one-packet lag), so that window is normally recoverable; the word 'only if' understates the guarantee that the fixture demonstrates.
findings.assessment: wording only; the safety claim is correct and conservative.

findings.observed: createdAt is deliberately retained across resume, and manifestPayloadSha256 is a digest over a payload that includes createdAt, so an otherwise-identical resumed run and fresh run never share manifest bytes or a payload digest (fixture observation: differences limited to manifest.json / manifestPayloadSha256 / createdAt).
findings.assessment: intended behaviour, not a defect; recorded because a reviewer comparing two runs without holding the clock constant would wrongly read the digest difference as nondeterminism.
